title: 1977 AHSME Problem 3
statement: A man has \(\$2.73\) in pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters and half dollars. If he has an equal number of coins of each kind, then the total number of coins he has is

solutions.text:
One coin of each kind is worth \(1+5+10+25+50=91\) cents. Since \(\frac{273}{91}=3,\) there are three coins of each of the five kinds, or \(5\cdot3=15\) coins.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Find the value of one coin of each of the five types
The five coins in one complete set are worth \(91\) cents
